chunks: Hammad narrated from Hariz who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Mufrid (one who performs Hajj al-Mufrad) who missed both the standing at Arafat and Muzdalifah. He said: 'He has until the sunrise of the Day of Nahr (10th of Dhul-Hijjah). If the sun rises on the Day of Nahr, he does not have a valid Hajj, and he makes it an Umrah, and he must perform Hajj next year.' I asked: 'What does he do?' He said: 'He performs Tawaf with the House, and (Sa'i) between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. If he wishes, he stays in Mecca; and if he wishes, he stays in Mina with the people; and if he wishes, he goes wherever he wishes, and he is not among the people in any (specific requirement).'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَانِ: The two standings (at Arafat and Muzdalifah)
key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: Hajj al-Mufrad (single Hajj, distinct from Tamattu or Qiran)
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Nahr (10th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses both Arafat and Muzdalifah during Hajj al-Mufrad?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific penalty for missing both Arafat and Muzdalifah during Hajj al-Mufrad, ruling that the Hajj becomes invalid and converts to Umrah, necessitating a return the following year. This highlights the critical status of Wuquf as a pillar (rukn) rather than merely a condition, distinguishing it from minor omissions. The Imam’s allowance for the pilgrim to remain in Mina or depart freely after completing the requisite Tawaf and Sa'i underscores the flexibility in post-ritual conduct once the core deficiency is acknowledged.
